newsitem.title: JAPAN: Key JGBs end slightly lower after setting new high.
newsitem.headline: Key JGBs end slightly lower after setting new high.

text.p: Key December Japanese government bond futures ended slightly lower on Friday after setting an all-time high earlier in the afternoon.
The December contract fell rapidly toward the close due to position adjustment sales ahead of a long weekend, a brokerage trader said.
Earlier, the December contract rose to 125.72, an all-time high for any benchmark futures contract.
Traders said the key futures contract was boosted in the afternoon by talk that agricultural cooperatives had bought cash JGBs.
A trader at a regional bank said there was also speculation in the market that public funds may begin buying JGBs soon.
The first trader said although he had not heard of purchases by public funds or agricultural financial institutions, there was some talk that other institutional investors had bought cash JGBs.
"I heard some people saying that trust banks, life insurers and city banks had bought JGBs," the brokerage trader said.
The December ended at 125.45, down slightly from Thursday's 125.48.
Turnover was 54,413 contracts.
City banks were detected selling cash JGBs in the morning, traders said.

"There were a number of large-lot sales in the morning. One city bank is said to have sold a total of about 200 billion yen worth of the benchmark JGB and government-guaranteed and municipal bonds," a trust bank trader said.
Some in the market seem eager to rid themselves of government-guaranteed and municipal bonds with coupon rates of around three percent, the trader said.
"They are selling to take profit... I think there is also the sense that they'd rather be holding JGBs," he said.
The benchmark 182nd cash JGB stood at 2.520 percent as of 0706 GMT, unchanged from Thursday.
Traders said the market was having trouble digesting some of the corporate bonds issued this week.
On Thursday, Tokyo Electric Power Co Inc (TEPCO) launched a 2.8 percent 150 billion yen 10-year bond and a 3.45 percent 50 billion yen 20-year bond.

"TEPCO's 20-year bond was easily absorbed by the market, but dealers are said to be having a more difficult time finding buyers for the company's 10-year bonds," said a trader at a city bank's securities unit.
"The TEPCO bonds could be a second coming of the 2.9 percent JGBs," the trust bank trader said.

Everyone had said they did not want the most recently issued 190th 10-year JGBs, which had a coupon rate of 2.9 percent, but demand picked up later on and they now have a yield of less than 2.7 percent, the trader said.
Monday is a national holiday and markets will be closed. -- Masayuki Kitano, Tokyo Treasury Desk +81-3-5473-3748
